summary: Five roles reach the shortlist, four permanent and one freelance: voize's freelance Senior Backend Engineer in Kotlin (health-tech, remote from Germany, on the employer's own Ashby board), Scento's Staff Full-Stack Engineer (Next.js/Medusa, remote in the EU, EUR 140-185k stated), eventfirst's Senior Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript, AI; its earlier ad died, this is a new one), HeroSoftware's Senior Full Stack (EUR 50-80k, German at native level) and Cito's full-stack role (Django and React with LLM agents, remote DACH). Nothing asks for Italian again; Modash's EUR 80-110k role is re-advertised but stays kept because its Workable location list excluded Germany. The profile changed only by a source note since the last sweep, so the six roles shortlisted on 2026-10-28 to 10-30 were not re-judged; JetBrains' and Haufe's are still live and come up for re-checking tomorrow. Review: 4 shortlisted roles demoted to kept (voize: Kotlin required, none on the CV; Scento: several years at staff or principal level; HeroSoftware: native-level German; Cito: Python/Django required, none on the CV), 5 pay projections re-based on JobRise pages re-read (voize widened, eventfirst, Cito, ElevenLabs and Valsoft), voize gap corrected (3-month minimum is in the Ashby ad), link checks redone for 7 postings; eventfirst remains the only shortlisted role.
open_questions: Several good postings ask for German "auf Muttersprachenniveau" (HeroSoftware) or C1/C2 (voize, Haufe Lexware): is that a gap to flag and still shortlist, or should native-level German be a drop reason?
Recruiter ads that re-publish the same role for a year (IESF: datePosted 2025-08-29, new join.com id every few weeks) look current on any date check: should they count as `stale`, as this sweep did?

postings.title: Freelance Senior Backend Engineer - Kotlin (m/f/d)
postings.why: Health-tech scale-up (voice documentation for care staff) hiring a freelance backend engineer for its German-market squad: REST integrations between its platform and partners' care and hospital software, in Kotlin; remote from Germany, France or the UK.
postings.gap: "Excellent proficiency with Kotlin" is the one language the ad names, and Kotlin appears nowhere on the CV (Java only), so the hard requirement is not met; "Several years of experience in backend development and API integration" (met); "Fluent in German (C1)" (met); "Willingness and work authorisation to travel to Berlin"; "Can work with us for minimum 3+ months" (stated in the Ashby ad itself); no day rate stated.

pay_estimate.basis: No rate in the ad (Ashby compensation empty). JobRise 'Freelance Developer Deutschland 2026: Stundensätze' (20 May 2026, re-read in review): Kotlin Backend EUR 90-125 an hour, Senior Developer EUR 85-120, Java Spring Boot EUR 85-120, net B2B rates (EUR 720-1,000 a day at 8 h). FRATCH city pages (search snippet, not re-opened): Spring developers EUR 60-111 an hour, interim Kotlin in Frankfurt EUR 510-910 a day. A blog and an AI-generated platform page, so the range is wide.
